subQuestions.questionText: The quantity of the product which can be purchased by consumers at a given price:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Demand is defined as the quantity of a product that consumers are willing and able to purchase at a given price during a specific time period.

subQuestions.questionText: A situation in the market where the price of goods is held constant regardless of the cost of production is known as price …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Price fixing is when the price of goods is held constant regardless of production cost. It typically occurs in controlled markets.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is a guideline for packaging fresh produce:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Produce should fit well inside the container to prevent damage during transport. Packaging should include product info (not exclude it), should not contain harmful chemicals, and containers should be sturdy (not soft).

options.A: Package must not include information about the produce
options.C: Container should be soft for easy handling
options.D: Produce should fit well inside the container

subQuestions.questionText:
The following occurs in a market when the price of a product is high:
(i) The demand is high and the supply is low
(ii) The demand is low and the supply is high
(iii) The more the products, the more producers are willing to sell
(iv) The willingness to buy a product decreases

Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
(ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct. When prices are high: demand decreases (low) while supply increases (high), more products mean producers are more willing to sell, and consumers' willingness to buy decreases. Statement (i) is incorrect.

subQuestions.questionText: An economic concept where production output does not increase at the same rate as fertiliser application increases:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The Law of diminishing returns states that as one input (fertiliser) is increased while others are held constant, the marginal output will eventually decrease — output does not keep increasing at the same rate.

subQuestions.questionText: A financial record showing the receipts and payments over a given period:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
A cash flow statement shows the actual receipts (money in) and payments (money out) over a given period. A budget is a plan, an income statement shows profit/loss, and a balance sheet shows assets/liabilities at a point in time.

subQuestions.questionText: The management principle which involves the evaluation of plans and remediation to achieve the set goals:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Control is the management principle that evaluates whether plans are being followed and applies remediation/corrective action to achieve set goals.

subQuestions.questionText:
Labourers can cause losses in a production enterprise if they are not …
(i) skilled in their job.
(ii) supervised.
(iii) motivated.
(iv) experiencing work related challenges.

Choose the CORRECT combination.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
(i), (ii) and (iii) — labourers cause losses when they are NOT skilled, NOT supervised, and NOT motivated. Statement (iv) is logically inverted: workers who ARE experiencing challenges (not 'not experiencing') would cause losses.

subQuestions.questionText: The illustration below shows a breeding system known as … (Refer to the illustration showing horse × donkey = mule in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Species crossing (interspecific hybridisation) is shown — a horse and donkey (different species) are crossed to produce a mule. This differs from crossbreeding (different breeds within same species) or inbreeding (closely related individuals).

subQuestions.questionText: A modification technique where a gene gun is used to fire bullets coated with desired genes is known as …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Biolistic (also called particle bombardment or gene gun method) is the genetic modification technique where microscopic bullets/particles coated with DNA are fired into target cells.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term from COLUMN B that matches the description: 'Quantity of products supplied exceeds quantity demanded'.
COLUMN B: A) sex-linked, B) grant, C) surplus, D) interpersonal, E) mass marketing, F) shortage, G) financial, H) height
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — surplus (2 marks)
A surplus exists when supply exceeds demand at a given price.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term from COLUMN B that matches the description: 'Marketing approach that promotes and sells the same product in different ways to different groups of consumers'.
COLUMN B: A) sex-linked, B) grant, C) surplus, D) interpersonal, E) mass marketing, F) shortage, G) financial, H) height
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: E — mass marketing (2 marks)
Mass marketing involves promoting and selling the same product to different consumer groups using varied marketing approaches.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term from COLUMN B that matches the description: 'The funding provided for a specific purpose and not repaid'.
COLUMN B: A) sex-linked, B) grant, C) surplus, D) interpersonal, E) mass marketing, F) shortage, G) financial, H) height
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B — grant (2 marks)
A grant is funding given for a specific purpose that does not need to be repaid (unlike a loan).

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term from COLUMN B that matches the description: 'A management skill that needs a farmer to understand taxation and interest rates'.
COLUMN B: A) sex-linked, B) grant, C) surplus, D) interpersonal, E) mass marketing, F) shortage, G) financial, H) height
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: G — financial (2 marks)
Financial management skills require understanding of taxation, interest rates, budgeting and other money matters.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term from COLUMN B that matches the description: 'A characteristic represented by X^h Y with X^H X^h-genotype'.
COLUMN B: A) sex-linked, B) grant, C) surplus, D) interpersonal, E) mass marketing, F) shortage, G) financial, H) height
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A — sex-linked (2 marks)
The notation $X^H X^h$ and $X^h Y$ uses superscripts on the X chromosome, indicating the gene is carried on the sex chromosome — a sex-linked characteristic.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: The process of attracting consumers to a specific product through various forms of communication.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Promotion (accept advertising)
[Award 2 marks for either correct term]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: A measure of production output in the labour force.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Labour productivity
[Award 2 marks for the correct term]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: The genetic characteristics that give rise to a range of phenotypes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Quantitative
[Award 2 marks — quantitative characteristics show continuous variation/range of phenotypes]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: An individual that has different alleles for a particular gene on each homologous chromosome.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Heterozygous
[Award 2 marks — heterozygous individuals carry two different alleles for a gene]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: A type of risk which occurs when genes from genetically modified crops are transferred to wild plants making them herbicide resistant.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Environmental (risk)
[Award 2 marks — gene flow to wild plants is classified as an environmental risk of GMOs]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: In 'controlled' marketing, products from individual producers are placed together, graded and handled as one mass.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Cooperative
[Award 1 mark — cooperative marketing is when products from many producers are pooled, graded and handled as one mass. Controlled marketing involves government regulation, which is different.]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: A list of assets on the farm is known as 'liability'.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Inventory
[Award 1 mark — an inventory is a list of assets. Liabilities are debts/obligations.]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: The law of 'dominance' states that an organism possesses two alleles which separate so that each gamete receives only one allele.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Segregation
[Award 1 mark — Mendel's law of segregation states that paired alleles separate during gamete formation. The law of dominance refers to dominant alleles masking recessive ones.]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: 'Artificial' selection is where only individuals that are best suited to the environment survive.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Natural
[Award 1 mark — natural selection is where organisms best suited to the environment survive (Darwin). Artificial selection is human-controlled selection for desired traits.]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: 'Biometrics' is the degree to which a characteristic is determined mostly by genes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Heritability
[Award 1 mark — heritability measures how much of a characteristic is due to genetics. Biometrics is the statistical measurement of biological data.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the following in the schematic representation above:
(a) Marketing system E
(b) Marketing channel A
(Refer to the schematic showing channels A: products sold directly to retailer, B: products sold at point of production, C: livestock sold to highest bidder, D: goods delivered to an agent who sells on behalf of farmer, with E representing the overall system.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Marketing system E - Free marketing (1 mark)
(b) Marketing channel A - Direct / contract marketing (1 mark)
[Award 1 mark per correct identification]
subQuestions.topic: Agricultural Marketing - Marketing Systems and Channels

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the letter (A–E) that represents the marketing channel that matches EACH of the following descriptions:
(a) The farmer has to pay commission
(b) No transport costs by the farmer
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) D (1 mark) — agent sells on behalf of the farmer for a commission
(b) B (1 mark) — products sold at the point of production, so no transport needed
[Award 1 mark per correct letter]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO disadvantages of the marketing system identified in QUESTION 2.1.1(a).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO disadvantages of free marketing:
• Farmers are likely to experience price fluctuations
• High marketing/production costs
• The producer has limited bargaining power
• The producer runs a risk because wrong production decisions may lead to greater financial loss
• Producers may set the price artificially
• There is a risk of product rejection if not accepted by consumers
• Cartels are formed and consumers/other suppliers are exploited
• Over production can lead to big surplus
• Farmers may lack the necessary skills
• Farmers bear all the risk alone
• Small scale farmers struggle to keep up production as they focus on marketing
• Competition is high for individual farmers
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the product with the demand that is:
(a) Price inelastic
(b) Price elastic
(Refer to the table showing Product A: Price 1 = R10/200 bags, Price 2 = R15/100 bags; Product B: Price 1 = R20/200 bags, Price 2 = R25/190 bags.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Inelastic - Product B (1 mark) — small change in demand (200 to 190) despite price increase (R20 to R25)
(b) Elastic - Product A (1 mark) — large change in demand (200 to 100) with price increase (R10 to R15)
[Award 1 mark per correct answer]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.2.1(a).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The change in price
Mark 2: has little influence on the quantity of product demanded
[Award 2 marks for a complete answer linking price change to small change in demand]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that might have resulted in price elasticity of the product identified in QUESTION 2.2.1(b).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following factors:
• Nature of the product
• Availability of substitute products
• Consumers' income
• Fuel costs
• Time period / seasonality
• Price
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Deduce a problem associated with each factor above that may hamper the marketing of agricultural products as represented below:
(a) Picture A (Transportation)
(b) Picture B (Storage)
(Refer to Picture A showing transportation truck and Picture B showing storage of produce in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Picture A - Wide distribution of production areas and distance to markets / poor infrastructure / accidents / theft / delays / transportation costs (1 mark)
(b) Picture B - Perishability / spoilage / storage costs (1 mark)
[Award 1 mark per correct problem]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate how the problem in QUESTION 2.3.1(a) could be addressed to ensure an improved agri-business chain.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Any ONE of the following:
• Improving road infrastructure
• Provision of security
• Insurance
• Production closer to markets
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate ONE cost factor aligned to Picture B that may have an impact on the marketing of the agricultural product.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Supply of energy / electricity / storage costs
[Award 1 mark for any one correct cost factor related to storage]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO roles of legislation in the effective marketing of agricultural products.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Promoting / optimising efficient marketing of products
• Increasing market accessibility to all participants
• Enhancing the viability of agricultural sector
• Controls the sale and export of certain agricultural products
• Promotes meat safety at abattoirs
• Controls the export of perishable products from South Africa
• Promotes a fair / sustainable market place for consumer products and services
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a bar graph showing the quantities of wheat supplied and demanded from 2018 to 2022. (Refer to the table in the question paper showing data: 2018 supply 180/demand 230; 2019 supply 190/demand 210; 2020 supply 200/demand 175; 2021 supply 220/demand 165; 2022 supply 250/demand 140 — all in tons.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Marking criteria/rubric (award 1 mark each, total 6 marks):
Mark 1: Correct heading (e.g. 'The supply and demand of wheat from 2018 to 2022')
Mark 2: X-axis correctly calibrated with label (Years)
Mark 3: Y-axis correctly calibrated with label (Quantities supplied and demanded)
Mark 4: Correct unit (tons)
Mark 5: Bar graph (not line/other type) — must show two bars per year for supply and demand
Mark 6: Accuracy — at least 80% correctly plotted

Data to plot:
2018: Supply 180, Demand 230
2019: Supply 190, Demand 210
2020: Supply 200, Demand 175
2021: Supply 220, Demand 165
2022: Supply 250, Demand 140

subQuestions.questionText:
Deduce from the table above the trend of each of the following over a period of five years:
(a) Quantities supplied
(b) Quantities demanded
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Supply (1 mark): Quantities supplied increased from 180 tons (2018) to 250 tons (2022)
(b) Demand (1 mark): Quantities demanded decreased from 230 tons (2018) to 140 tons (2022)
[Award 1 mark per correct trend with reference to figures]

subQuestions.questionText: A group of farmers started a milling project to assist people from the surrounding areas to grind maize into maize meal. They organised a milling machine and other relevant equipment. Then they started the business with five workers. The business grew very fast and within a period of two years they had fifteen workers. Identify TWO phases of entrepreneurship in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Identification of a business opportunity
• Determining the resources required / resource mobilization
• Starting the business
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name the marketing function in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Processing
[Award 1 mark — converting raw maize into maize meal is the processing marketing function]

subQuestions.questionText: Give an advantage of the marketing function named in QUESTION 2.5.2 for the community.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: It provides job / skill opportunities (for the community)
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE purpose of a SWOT analysis in a business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: It helps to evaluate the business
[Award 1 mark — accept similar formulations such as 'identify strengths/weaknesses/opportunities/threats to inform planning']

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the letter (A–D) representing the statement that addresses EACH of the following aspects of the SWOT analysis:
(a) Opportunity
(b) Threat
(c) Weakness
(d) Strength
(Statements: A - The farmer lacks capital and management skills; B - Increasing interest rates render enterprise less competitive; C - New markets are opening; D - The farmer has a lot of land.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Opportunity - C (1 mark) — new markets opening is an external opportunity
(b) Threat - B (1 mark) — increasing interest rates is an external threat
(c) Weakness - A (1 mark) — lack of capital/skills is an internal weakness
(d) Strength - D (1 mark) — having a lot of land is an internal strength
[Award 1 mark per correct letter]

In the list above, identify the production factor where each of the following is applicable:
(a) Used as collateral
(b) Used to pay the salaries of farm workers
(c) The farmer
(List: A - Capital, B - Management, C - Land, D - Labour)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Land / C (1 mark) — land is commonly used as collateral due to its appreciating value
(b) Capital / A (1 mark) — money/capital is used to pay salaries
(c) Management / B (1 mark) — the farmer is the manager of the enterprise
[Award 1 mark per correct answer]

subQuestions.questionText: Justify the answer to QUESTION 3.1.1(a).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Any ONE of the following:
• The value of land appreciates
• Easy to sell / transfer / convert
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the economic characteristic of land illustrated in the table above. (Refer to the table showing population growth from 24 million (1983) to 44 million (2023) while arable land decreased from 12 million ha to 4 million ha in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Land for agricultural purposes is scarce / limited / limitedness

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO functions of land that are evident in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for the following:
• Provides space for agricultural production / activities
• Provides food for humans / feeding for animals
[Award 2 marks total]

subQuestions.questionText: HIV/Aids has a negative impact on the productivity of farm workers. Indicate TWO implications of HIV/Aids for the agricultural sector.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Productivity will decrease
• Knowledge / experience / skills are lost
• Makes planning difficult
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE measure farmers can take to address the problem of HIV/Aids on the farm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Any ONE of the following:
• Awareness campaigns / education
• Access to anti-retroviral medication
• Access to treatment for STDs
• Education in acceptable moral behaviour
• Access to condoms
• Establish support groups
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify, in the list of personnel above, an example of each of the following:
(a) Casual worker
(b) Manager
(c) Unskilled worker
(d) Skilled worker
(Personnel: A dairy foreman; Two general workers; A brick-layer; An electronic feeding machine operator)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Casual worker - Brick-layer (1 mark)
(b) Manager - Dairy foreman (1 mark)
(c) Unskilled worker - General workers (1 mark)
(d) Skilled worker - Electronic feeding machine operator / brick layer (1 mark)
[Award 1 mark per correct identification]

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the legislation that regulates each of the following:
(a) Payment as a result of an accident in a work place
(b) Provision of security when workers become unemployed
(c) Hours of work, leave and working on public holidays
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act / COIDA (Act 130 of 1993) (1 mark)
(b) Unemployment Insurance Act / UIA (Act 66 of 2001) (1 mark)
(c) Basic Conditions of Employment Act / BCEA (Act 75 of 1997) (1 mark)
[Award 1 mark per correct Act]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of financial record represented in the table above. (Refer to the table showing expected expenditure (Irrigation R10 300, Manure R22 400, Fuel R13 300, Labour R24 500, Potting soil R8 800, Vegetative material R45 500, Chemicals R18 700) and expected income (Flowers shop R150 000, Flowers nursery R40 000, Compost R7 500) for a horticultural enterprise.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Enterprise budget
[Award 1 mark — this records expected income and expenditure for a single enterprise]

subQuestions.questionText: Use a formula to calculate the profit or loss of this enterprise. (Show ALL calculations.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct formula: Profit/Loss = Total income − Total expenditure
Mark 2: Correct total income: $R150\,000 + R40\,000 + R7\,500 = R197\,500$
Mark 3: Correct total expenditure: $R10\,300 + R22\,400 + R13\,300 + R24\,500 + R8\,800 + R45\,500 + R18\,700 = R143\,500$ AND correct substitution: $R197\,500 - R143\,500$
Mark 4: Correct final answer: $= R54\,000$ (profit)
[Award 4 marks total]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the farmer should continue or not with the enterprise.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The farmer should continue
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 3.5.3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The enterprise made a profit of R54 000
[Award 1 mark for a reason that references the profit/positive financial outcome]

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the curve (A or B) that represents the following:
(a) Movable capital assets
(b) Fixed capital assets
(Refer to the graph showing curve A starting high and decreasing over time, and curve B starting low and increasing over time, on Value of assets vs Time axes.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Movable capital assets - A (1 mark) — depreciate over time (decreasing curve)
(b) Fixed capital assets - B (1 mark) — appreciate over time (increasing curve)
[Award 1 mark per correct identification]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason to support the answer to QUESTION 3.6.1(b).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The value of the fixed assets appreciates (over time)
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO problems of capital as a production factor.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Depreciation
• Scarcity / shortage of capital
• Expensive / high cost
• Over-capitalization
• Under-capitalization
• Risk factor
• High interest rate / interest rate may change
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO types of risks that can influence a farming business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for the following:
• Internal
• External
[Award 2 marks total]

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO sources of risks in farming businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Technical risks
• Market and price risks
• Financial risks
• Legal risks
• Production risks
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO risk management strategies.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for the following:
• Diversification
• Risk sharing
[Award 2 marks total]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the pattern of inheritance in the diagram above. (Refer to the diagram showing P1: BB (black bull) × WW (white cow) → F1: all BW (grey); F1 × F1 → F2: BB, BW, BW, WW (white) in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Incomplete dominance
[Award 1 mark — neither black nor white is fully dominant; heterozygous offspring are grey (intermediate)]

subQuestions.questionText: Justify the answer to QUESTION 4.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The F1 offspring have intermediate characteristic (grey is intermediate between black and white)
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText:
Label each of the following represented in the diagram above:
(a) Process by 1
(b) Genotype by 2
(c) Phenotype 3
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) 1 - Meiosis (1 mark) — process producing the gametes (B and W)
(b) 2 - BW (1 mark) — genotype of the heterozygous offspring
(c) 3 - Black (1 mark) — phenotype corresponding to genotype BB
[Award 1 mark per correct label]

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down each of the following:
(a) Genotypic ratio of the F1-generation
(b) Phenotypic ratio of the F2-generation
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Genotypic ratio of F1 - 1 (or 4) (1 mark) — all offspring are BW (a single genotype, ratio 1 or all 4)
(b) Phenotypic ratio of F2 - 1 black : 2 grey : 1 white (1 mark)
[Award 1 mark per correct ratio]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the genetic phenomenon represented by the data in the table above. (Refer to the table showing genetically identical tomato seeds yielding different harvests in three provinces: Province 1: 35 tons, Province 2: 20 tons, Province 3: 60 tons.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Variation
[Award 1 mark — the same genotype produced different phenotypes (yields) in different environments, illustrating variation]

subQuestions.questionText: State THREE possible causes of the phenomenon that could have led to the results in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any THREE environmental causes of variation:
• Nutrition
• Rainfall / water supply
• Soil factors
• Temperature
• Topography
• Light intensity
• Diseases / pests
[Maximum 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Match the types of mutagenic agents (chemical; biological; physical) with their effects below:
(a) Abnormal cell division resulting in polyploidy caused by colchicine
(b) Radiation such as X-rays damages the DNA molecule and causes it to break
(c) Bacteria cause inflammation that releases chemicals which damage the DNA molecule
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Chemical (1 mark) — colchicine is a chemical mutagen
(b) Physical (1 mark) — radiation/X-rays are physical mutagens
(c) Biological (1 mark) — bacteria are biological mutagens
[Award 1 mark per correct match]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the most accurate method used by farmers to select animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Pedigree selection
[Award 1 mark — pedigree selection uses ancestor records and is considered the most accurate]

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE other method that is used by farmers to select animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Any ONE of the following:
• Mass selection
• Progeny selection
• Family selection
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why variation in selection and breeding is important.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Any ONE of the following:
• Variation is the basis for selection
• Helps animals to adapt to the changing environment
• Used to improve crop varieties and livestock breeds
• For the development of new cultivars / breeds
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between crossbreeding and inbreeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Inbreeding is the crossing of closely related animals
Mark 2: Crossbreeding is the crossing of non-related animals (or animals of different breeds)
[Award 2 marks for a complete differentiation showing both terms]

subQuestions.questionText: In goats, the allele for black fur (B) is dominant over the allele for brown fur (b). A brown-furred goat is crossed with a heterozygous black-furred goat. Use a Punnett square to determine the genotype of the F1-generation offspring.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marking rubric (award 1 mark each, total 4 marks):
Mark 1: Correct gametes of parent one (heterozygous black: B and b)
Mark 2: Correct gametes of parent two (homozygous brown: b and b)
Mark 3: Correct genotypes of the offspring (Bb, Bb, bb, bb)
Mark 4: Punnett square correctly populated with gametes and offspring

Expected Punnett square:
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 & B & b \\
\hline
b & Bb & bb \\
b & Bb & bb \\
\end{array}

F1 genotypes: 2 Bb : 2 bb

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of black-furred goats.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct setup: $\frac{2}{4} \times 100$
Mark 2: Correct answer: $= 50\%$
[Award 2 marks total — 2 black (Bb) out of 4 offspring = 50%]

subQuestions.questionText: The length of mohair in goats is controlled by two pairs of genes. The base length for a recessive goat is aabb which is 25 cm long. Each additive allele contributes 3 cm to the base length. Identify the pattern of inheritance controlling the length of mohair in goats.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Polygenic inheritance
[Award 1 mark — multiple genes (two pairs) control a single trait, which is polygenic inheritance]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 4.6.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The length of mohair is controlled by more than one pair of genes
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the length of mohair in goats with genotype AABb.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct setup showing base length and additive alleles: AABb has 3 dominant (additive) alleles, so length = $25 \text{ cm} + 3 \text{ cm} + 3 \text{ cm} + 3 \text{ cm}$
Mark 2: Correct final answer: $= 34 \text{ cm}$
[Award 2 marks total]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate another genotype of goats with mohair of the same length as the one in QUESTION 4.6.3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: AaBB
[Award 1 mark — also has 3 dominant (additive) alleles giving 25 + 3(3) = 34 cm]

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term genetic modification.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Genetic modification is the technique of changing / manipulation of the genetic characteristics of an organism
Mark 2: by inserting the genes from another organism into its DNA
[Award 2 marks for a complete definition mentioning both manipulation of genes AND insertion from another organism]

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO aims of genetic modification of plants and animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Improving the yield
• Improve the tolerance to environmental conditions
• Improve the resistance to pests, diseases and weeds
• Improve the flavour and shelf-life of produce
• Increasing the nutritional value of crops / animal products
• Producing pharmaceutical crops / develop new vaccines / medicines
• Develop animal models for studies of diseases
• Increasing genetic diversity
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE advantage of genetic modification over the traditional method.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Any ONE of the following:
• It is precise
• It is fast
• Not limited to organisms of the same species
[Award 1 mark]
